steps.description: Run DESeq() on the T1S1 object (design ~ batch + condition) and extract the Wald-test contrast condition: treated vs control with independent filtering and BH FDR. Write the full result table for every tested gene (gene symbol, baseMean, log2FC raw, lfcSE, shrunken log2FC, stat, pvalue, padj) sorted by padj, plus a filtered table at padj < 0.05, and separately note how many of those also exceed |log2FC| > 1. The batch-adjusted model is the reported result.

steps.context: Downstream interpretation of the treated vs control kidney contrast. Needs human gene-set collections keyed by gene symbol — a hallmark collection and a GO biological-process collection for Homo sapiens. Both appear to be provisioned in this environment, but the step must resolve them at run time rather than assume a path.
steps.question: Which biological processes and hallmark states are coordinately shifted between treated and control kidney samples, according to the batch-adjusted DE ranking?
constraints: Use human gene sets only — the kidney samples are Homo sapiens (taxon 9606)
Rank on the full tested gene list, not on the FDR-filtered subset
Use the ~12,000 tested genes as the background universe for any over-representation test, never the full genome
Collapse redundant GO terms before reporting how many processes are enriched
steps.description: Take the full T1S2 result table (all tested genes, HGNC symbols) and build a ranked list from the DESeq2 Wald statistic (or -log10(p) signed by the shrunken log2FC if the statistic is unavailable), dropping genes with NA statistics and resolving duplicate symbols by keeping the most extreme value. Run fgsea (multilevel) against human hallmark gene sets and human GO biological-process gene sets, restricting to sets with 15-500 members after intersection with the ~12,000 tested symbols. Report normalised enrichment scores with BH-adjusted p-values, collapse redundant GO parent/child hits before quoting a count, and write enrichment tables plus a bar/dot plot of the top pathways in each collection and leading-edge gene lists for the top sets. Additionally run an over-representation test on the padj<0.05 gene list from T1S2 against the same collections, using all tested genes as the background universe — but only if that list has at least 15 genes; otherwise state that ORA was skipped for lack of hits and rely on the ranked GSEA.
acceptance_criteria: A ranked-list GSEA table with NES and BH-adjusted p-values is written for each gene-set collection used
The gene-set collections actually used are named in the output, with their organism confirmed as human
The size of the ranked list and the number of gene sets passing the 15-500 size filter after universe intersection are reported
Leading-edge genes are reported for the top enriched sets
If a gene-set resource cannot be resolved, the step says so explicitly and reports on whichever collection it did resolve, rather than substituting a different organism

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch in model
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single bulk RNA-seq count matrix (12,000 gene symbols x 12 human kidney samples, raw integer salmon counts) with a sample table carrying `condition` (6 treated vs 6 control) and `batch` (two processing batches). Because the design is balanced — each batch holds both conditions — batch is an estimable nuisance covariate, not a confounder, so the correct treatment is to include it as a fixed effect in the DESeq2 design (~ batch + condition) rather than to pre-correct counts with ComBat and then test corrected values, which would understate residual variance and inflate significance. T1S1 verifies the design is genuinely balanced (2x2 cross-tabulation, sample-name concordance between the two CSVs), filters low-count genes, builds the DESeq2 object with the additive design, and produces QC diagnostics (VST PCA coloured by condition and batch, sample-sample distances, library sizes) so the actual magnitude of the batch effect relative to the treatment effect is measured rather than assumed. T1S2 runs the Wald test for treated vs control with batch in the model, applies apeglm LFC shrinkage for ranking, writes the full result table plus the FDR-filtered gene list, and — as a sensitivity check on the modelling decision, not as the primary result — refits without the batch term and reports the overlap, so the reader can see what the covariate bought. n=6 per group is modest; the step must report the number of genes passing FDR 0.05 plainly and refrain from framing a small hit count as a negative result. T2S1 takes the ranked gene list forward into fgsea over human hallmark and GO-BP sets; enrichment is interpretive and is kept off the critical path, so if the gene-set resource is not resolvable at run time the step reports that and the DE result still stands.
